takeaway: They practise in thousands of slightly different simulated worlds at once, so the real world is just one more variation.

selfCheck.question: Why vary the worlds instead of building one perfect copy of the real one?
selfCheck.answer: no copy is ever perfect; real ground, weight, bumps differ; one-world robot slips; thousands of floors, weights and shoves -> real floor is just another.

sentence: Robots can learn to walk by practising in a computer simulation. Thousands of copies practise at the same time, each in a slightly different world, so the robot learns to handle almost anything, and the real world becomes just one more variation it can cope with.
